claims.reason: The same code does appear twice, but it is routine unit packaging, not repeated mathematical reasoning. The shared part is: call the matrix lemma, rebuild K₁,K₁i,e₁,e₁' and K₂,K₂i,e₂,e₂' as units, pair the integrality facts into K0 membership, and close the equation with Units.ext, Units.val_mul, coe_diagSnd_piK and the lemma's final equation. That is about six lines in each proof. All the mathematics (the Smith-type decomposition) is already in Matrix.exists_eq_mul_diagonal_mul_of_forall_mem_adicCompletionIntegers. The proposed lemma would be a thin unit-level wrapper around that existing API, which the rubric excludes. The nontrivial parts of each caller do not overlap. In exists_mem_K0_eq_latticeMap_mul_diagSnd, hpYi, hYi and hpY come from lattice-sandwich arguments with latticeMap_mono. In exists_ψ_nv_eq they come from local_of_mem_primeHeckeSet and adelic evaluation. A wrapper over units would be sound: Y⁻¹'s underlying matrix is definitionally φ(ev(n⁻¹)), and the lemma's hypotheses could be restated for Y and Y⁻¹. Even so, it would save only a handful of boilerplate lines (the packaging plus the h1/h2 or e1/e2 inverse facts) and would not isolate any repeated mathematical idea. It is a possible cosmetic tidy-up but does not meet the repeated-machinery bar.
